clue.text: A miracle here: Soviet approval for a capitalist country

parts.note: Cana in Galilee is where the Gospel says water was turned into wine
da is Russian for yes

explanation.surface: A Soviet nod for a capitalist nation would be a miracle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitalist' is a pun: the country has a capital (Ottawa), not necessarily a market economy.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a nation with a capital city, Ottawa, which is the pun in the clue.

clue.text: Charlie once so called in France

definitions.text: Charlie once so called in France

parts.words: Charlie once so called in France
parts.note: a Victorian music-hall song celebrated a bon viveur nicknamed after a French sparkling wine region

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' suggests a NATO alphabet C, but it refers to the music-hall song 'Champagne Charlie'; the name is also a region in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of north-east France gives its name to sparkling wine and to the song's hero.

clue.text: Holding up a Paris street? Nobody would have the nerve

indicators.note: would have says the word for nobody contains the other piece

parts.note: none means nobody

indicators.note: in a down clue holding up says the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: Nobody would dare to hold up traffic on a Paris street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding up' turns RUE into EUR, and 'would have' places it inside NONE. 'have the nerve' misleads: it means a nerve cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurone is a nerve cell, the basic unit of the nervous system.

clue.text: Fall of dusk marred fabulous forewarning of invasion

indicators.note: fall of suggests the letters of the next words collapse and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nightfall was spoiled by a legendary warning of attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall of' rearranges DUSKMARRED. Legend says Sir Francis Drake's drum will sound if England is in danger, hence 'fabulous'.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend holds that Drake's drum beats to warn of England's peril from invaders.

clue.text: Protector for a new rose stem

indicators.note: new says the letters of the two words are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener buys something to guard a freshly grown rose stem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ROSESTEM. Edward Seymour, Duke of Somerset, ruled England as Lord Protector for the boy king Edward VI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Somerset held the title Lord Protector during the minority of Edward VI.

clue.text: Have more old-fashioned character

parts.note: out means out of fashion
a number is a numeral, a written character

explanation.surface: Someone has a more dated personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a written symbol, a numeral, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed in quantity is to have more than an opponent.

clue.text: Spikes Antony borrowed

definitions.meaning: the grain-bearing heads of cereal plants
Mark Antony says 'lend me your' in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar

explanation.definitionFit: Corn heads are its spikes; Antony asked the crowd to lend him their hearing organs.

clue.text: One's lifetime is hard, as Cervantes wrote

parts.note: span means the length of a life
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard on pencils

explanation.surface: A gloomy reflection that life is tough, in the style of Don Quixote's author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as Cervantes wrote' defines the language of the author of Don Quixote.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes wrote Don Quixote in the language of Spain.

clue.text: Sharp twist exposes some latent weakness

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An abrupt turn reveals a hidden flaw.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'exposes', but that word is the link between definition and hidden word, not part of the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a sudden sharp pull or twisting pinch.

clue.text: Its purpose is to eliminate excitement

definitions.meaning: a qualifying round of a race, which knocks out the slower runners

explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary race round weeds out competitors; warmth of feeling, as in the height of passion, is excitement.

clue.text: Consumed by almost fully-grown fawn

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so one piece follows the other
almost says the word for grown-up loses its final letter

parts.note: an adult is fully grown
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A nearly mature deer has been eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fawn' looks like a young deer, but it is the verb: to flatter servilely.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn on someone is to flatter them excessively, just as to adulate is to praise slavishly.

clue.text: Sauce made from weed — technique is concealed

indicators.note: is concealed says the word for technique is tucked within the word for weed

parts.note: tare is a weed, as in the biblical parable of wheat and tares
art means skill or technique

explanation.surface: A cook makes a sauce from weeds, keeping the method secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is concealed' puts ART inside TARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartare is a mayonnaise-based condiment with capers and gherkins, served with fish.

clue.text: Classical poet displays well-bred revulsion for courtship

parts.note: proper means respectable or well-bred

indicators.note: revulsion, read as a turning back, says the word for courtship is read backwards

parts.note: suit means wooing, as a suitor pays suit

explanation.surface: An ancient poet shows a refined person's distaste for wooing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revulsion' is read literally as a turning back, reversing SUIT to TIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Propertius was a Roman elegiac poet of the Augustan age.

clue.text: Like Blake's rose? Well, no

explanation.definitionFit: Blake's poem calls the rose ill, and someone not in good health is unwell.

clue.text: Dandy Spaniard has gold — his surplus goes in the bank

definitions.text: his surplus goes in the bank

parts.note: blood is an old word for a fashionable young man
Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A dashing Spanish gentleman has gold and banks the excess.
explanation.walkthrough: The bank is a blood bank, not a money one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gives spare blood has it stored in a hospital blood bank.

clue.text: Was he cut into jelly by Beowulf?

definitions.text: Was he cut into jelly by Beowulf?

indicators.note: into says the word for cut goes inside the word for jelly

parts.note: gel is a jelly-like substance
rend means tear or cut

explanation.surface: A question about a monster being hacked to pulp by the epic hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts REND inside GEL. The whole clue also describes the monster Beowulf maimed, tearing off his arm.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old English epic, Beowulf fights the monster Grendel and tears off his arm.

clue.text: Series of shots at the last minute from one side

parts.note: late means at a late time
a rally is an exchange of strokes in tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis exchange decided at the last moment from one end of the court.
explanation.definitionFit: Laterally means sideways, toward or from the flank.

clue.text: It sounds time to skip a page

parts.note: a bell rings out the hours
hop means skip or jump

explanation.surface: A ringing clock tells someone it is time to miss out a page of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'page' looks like a sheet of a book but is a hotel boy who runs errands.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a young attendant; in a hotel such an errand boy is called a bellboy.

clue.text: Extraction and distillation of neat grape

indicators.note: distillation of says the letters are processed and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A winemaking description of pressing and distilling grapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distillation of' rearranges NEATGRAPE. 'Extraction' means descent or lineage, not juicing.
explanation.definitionFit: One's extraction is one's ancestry or descent, i.e. family lineage.

clue.text: We are told tyre is on the back of the car

definitions.meaning: tyre sounds like tire, meaning to wear out

definitions.text: is on the back of the car
definitions.meaning: the pipe carrying fumes out at the rear of a vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: To tire is to wear out, a synonym; a car's fumes leave through a pipe at the rear.

clue.text: Distressing result of sitting in front of The Sweeney?'

definitions.text: Distressing result of sitting in front of The Sweeney?'

parts.words: Distressing result of sitting in front of The Sweeney?'
parts.note: de-tressing means losing locks; Sweeney Todd was the demon barber of Fleet Street, and The Sweeney is also a British TV police drama

explanation.walkthrough: 'Distressing' is read as de-tressing, removing hair; 'The Sweeney' suggests the British TV cop show, but means Sweeney Todd, the murderous barber.
explanation.definitionFit: A visit to a barber's chair ends with hair trimmed off.

clue.text: Make an anagram of 'command'

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as of does in 'speak of'
order means command

explanation.surface: An instruction to rearrange the letters of a word.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a puzzle instruction; in fact 'of' gives RE (concerning) and 'command' gives ORDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Making an anagram means putting letters in a new sequence, i.e. arranging them differently.

clue.text: In Attic township, over three-quarters is private land

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a deme was a township of ancient Attica, around Athens
S, N and E are three of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: In an Athenian village, more than three-quarters of the land is privately owned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-quarters' means three compass points, not a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is an estate kept by a lord for his own use, rather than let to tenants.

clue.text: Frisk the captain

definitions.meaning: to frisk is to gambol or caper about
short for skipper, the leader of a team or ship

explanation.definitionFit: Lambs gambol and caper, i.e. leap about; and a team or ship's captain is its skipper, shortened.

clue.text: Little girl responsible for a law barring her inheritance

parts.note: Sal is a short form of Sally
IC stands for in charge

explanation.surface: A small girl is behind a rule that stops her inheriting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Salic law, of Frankish origin, excluded women from succession to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salic law excluded females from royal succession, so a daughter could not inherit the crown.

clue.text: He may have to make a square out of an oval

definitions.text: He may have to make a square out of an oval

parts.words: He may have to make a square out of an oval
parts.note: the Oval is a London cricket ground, and the square is its central strip of pitches, prepared by the groundkeeper

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like geometry, but the Oval is a London cricket ground and the square is the prepared central area where pitches are cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundkeeper tends a sports field, including the cricket square at a ground like the Oval.

clue.text: Aloft, because in a tree

parts.note: up means aloft
as means because

explanation.surface: Something is high up because it is in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a Javanese tree with a poisonous sap.

clue.text: Where to draw properly

definitions.meaning: in a good or proper manner

explanation.definitionFit: Water is drawn from a shaft sunk in the ground; doing something rightly is doing it satisfactorily.

clue.text: Milky resin given to a duck

parts.note: lac is a resin secreted by insects, used for shellac
a teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: A white sap fed to a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacteal means relating to or resembling milk, from the Latin for milk.

clue.text: One would remember getting over this

definitions.text: One would remember getting over this

parts.words: One would remember getting over this
parts.note: recovering from a condition of lost memory would bring memories back

explanation.walkthrough: 'getting over' means recovering from; only on recovery would one remember.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is the condition, and recovering from it restores recall.

clue.text: Grazing animals always rejected this plant

parts.note: cattle are animals that graze

indicators.note: rejected says the word for always is sent back, so it reads backwards

parts.note: ay, also spelt aye, is an old word for ever or always

explanation.surface: Grazing livestock have never eaten a certain plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses AY to YA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattleya is a genus of showy tropical orchids.

clue.text: Move confidently along the block

definitions.meaning: to ... along is to move casually and assuredly
a lightweight building block made with cinders

explanation.definitionFit: To breeze along is to stroll with ease; a cinder building brick is called a breeze block.
